item.title: China’s 2026 moon laser communication speed is slower than Nasa’s in 2013
item.description: China has pulled off two-way laser communication between Earth and the moon, making it only the second nation after the United States to do so. But the data rates it achieved were well behind those recorded by Nasa more than a decade ago, and that has left space experts scratching their heads. Using telescopes in Yunnan province and an experimental satellite that is now orbiting the moon after a launch mishap in 2024, the team recorded a downlink speed of 100 megabits per second and an uplink... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Ling Xin

item.title: Scientists discover the key ingredients that make birdsong pretty
item.description: What makes birdsong beautiful? Answering this question could help us understand how soundscapes make the natural world relaxing for humans, opening the door to improving parks, upgrading the design of stressful places like waiting rooms and promoting conservation through birds with especially lovely songs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Community-led systems may curb illegal dumping in Indonesia's rural tourism areas
item.description: Local action may offer a model for waste management in rural tourism, according to research published in the International Journal of Tourism Anthropology. The study of waste problems in Kampung Nipah, a coastal tourism hamlet in North Sumatra, Indonesia, argues that rural communities with limited public services may need locally governed waste systems rather than relying solely on municipal services. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Children's picture books reflect changing attitudes to languages and can support revitalization
item.description: We know from a wealth of research that children's picture books support language learning. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Many space missions are searching for life beyond Earth, but are we prepared for the fallout if they succeed?
item.description: Microbes from space have fueled the plots of science fiction mainstays like "Project Hail Mary" and "The Andromeda Strain." But with more space missions launching each year, finding extraterrestrial life in a microbial form is becoming more plausible. What will the response be back here on Earth if—or when—scientists discover extraterrestrial microbes? Will the international policy and security communities be prepared for the fallout? Fuente: Phys.org.

Biologist Romi Castagnino examines the leading hypothesis behind the river’s extreme heat with the help of National Geographic Explorer and geothermal scientist Andrés Ruzo, who has spent years studying how the river gets so hot. | National Geographic

item.title: Border toy screening finds 12% exceed toxic-metal limits
item.description: Nearly four out of five children's toys purchased in the El Paso-Ciudad Juárez region contain at least one toxic element, according to a new study led by researchers at The University of Texas at El Paso. The findings, just published in the journal Environmental Pollution, represent the first binational screening of hazardous metals in toys sold on both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Magnetic beads streamline large-scale analysis of disease-linked glycopeptides
item.description: A research team has developed a reliable, economical laboratory method that uses tiny magnetic beads to study proteins with sugar molecules attached to them in blood and tissue samples. A better understanding of their pathological changes could help researchers diagnose and treat diseases, including cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New high-temperature, high-pressure isotope ratio analysis method developed for halogenated compounds
item.description: Halogenated organic compounds (HOCs) are widely used in industrial and consumer products, but some are highly persistent and difficult to analyze and manage. In a new study, researchers developed an innovative approach for carbon isotope ratio analysis of these compounds, which has previously been difficult. This approach will help track the sources and environmental pathways of such pollutants, contributing to the development of effective management strategies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Algorithm improves detection of differentially expressed genes in large single-cell trajectory data sets
item.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a method for measuring gene expression in individual cells, allowing observation of various cellular processes, including cell differentiation, the cell cycle and stimulus response, for each unique cell instead of averaging across millions of cells. It provides high-resolution snapshots of biological processes. However, it does not track the same cell continuously over time. To address this limitation, trajectory inference approaches have been developed that computationally arrange cellular snapshots along an inferred developmental trajectory known as… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Firelight may have sparked human storytelling by extending social hours
item.description: New research from the University of St Andrews has developed a novel hypothesis of how firelight was critical to the evolution of sophisticated storytelling. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Muddying the waters makes stickleback fish more coordinated, study finds
item.description: Stickleback fish can change their social behavior to help them find food in cloudy water, according to a new University of Bristol study published in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: LEDs let archaeologists see the past in a new light
item.description: An archaeological excavation is a little like eating a layered cake: Once you have removed a layer, you cannot put it back. The problem becomes even trickier if two layers look almost exactly the same. Researchers from Aarhus University and Moesgaard Museum in Denmark have now developed a relatively inexpensive multispectral imaging system that gives archaeologists more ways of looking at the soil before they dig into it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: ¿Ha adaptado Irán sus lanzacohetes para minar el estrecho de Ormuz?
item.description: Los bombardeos estadounidenses del domingo en la isla de Larak se justificaron por la necesidad de destruir nuevas capacidades para el minado del estrecho de Ormuz. El uso por parte de Irán de lanzacohetes para desplegar minas marinas en este paso estratégico sería algo sin precedentes, pero no imposible, aunque algunos expertos se muestran escépticos. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: France 24

item.title: Giant impact could have formed an intact moon within five hours, simulations suggest
item.description: New Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) modeling, conducted in collaboration with scientists at the University of Arizona, shows fundamental differences in how the moon may have formed from the giant impact that created the Earth–moon system. The new results used state-of-the-art computational techniques that factor in the material strength of the two colliding planets. These impact simulations could change how researchers understand moon formation and may help constrain the timing of the event. The research is published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Elementary school teachers report increased student hunger and anxiety after universal free school meals ended
item.description: A recent study published in the Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior explored elementary school teachers' experiences before and after the end of the federal universal free school meals (UFSM) policy. Researchers found that teachers perceived the policy had helped reduce student hunger and family stress, while its expiration was associated with increased hunger, anxiety about meal costs and decreased participation in school meal programs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Salt of the Earth: How Egypt's coastal sabkhas tell a story of climate and change
item.description: Have you ever walked across a salt flat so expansive it feels like another planet? That's what it's like standing in Egypt's coastal sabkhas—those otherworldly landscapes where the ground crunches beneath your feet and the air shimmers with heat. These aren't just barren wastelands; they're living laboratories that record the pulse of our changing climate. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Saturn encounter may have set distant centaur on path to becoming a comet
item.description: More than 3 billion miles (4.8 billion kilometers) from Earth, an ancient icy object is slowly awakening. As it drifts inward through the solar system, the frozen body known as Centaur 450P/LONEOS has begun releasing gas and dust—behavior more commonly associated with comets than with centaurs, the small icy objects that typically orbit between Jupiter and Neptune. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Canada's Labrador Shelf preserves climate records once thought erased by ice
item.description: The Labrador Shelf is a shallow marine area on the margin of the Labrador Sea in the North Atlantic off the east coast of Canada. During the last ice age, this region was covered by the Laurentide Ice Sheet, one of the largest ice masses in Earth's history, which once covered vast parts of North America. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A roadmap for animal-free chemical testing
item.description: For many years, the European Union has pursued a policy aimed at the replacement, reduction and refinement of animal testing (the 3Rs principle). To put the ethical principle of the 3Rs into practice, the European Commission has published a roadmap for the gradual phaseout of animal testing in the safety assessment of chemicals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A sustainable flame retardant derived from corn steep liquor
item.description: Certain phosphorus compounds are highly effective at suppressing fires, which is why they are widely used in flame retardants. Phosphorus, however, is a finite resource. Estimates suggest it could be depleted within the next 50–300 years. That is why, as part of the ScaleAmP project, a research team is working to extract phosphorus from corn steep liquor, a byproduct of starch production. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ocean heat waves linked with poorer health among children in coastal communities
item.description: Marine heat waves—periods of abnormally warm ocean temperatures—may have negative health effects on children who live in coastal communities in low- and middle-income countries, according to a study led by researchers at Penn State and the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: NASA awarded Blue Origin a contract Tuesday to develop the agency’s Mars Telecommunications Network, a next-generation communications system that will enable reliable, high-bandwidth communications and navigation services for current and future Mars missions. The firm-fixed-price contract has a maximum potential value of approximately $700 million to deliver a high-performance Mars telecommunications orbiter to NASA no […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: AI-informed AdaptiveFlow redefines large-scale cloud computing for drug discovery
item.description: Researchers today announced AdaptiveFlow, an AI-informed platform that can virtually screen billions of drug-like molecules with a 1,000-fold reduction in computational costs over existing methods. Developed and validated by scientists from St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, University of Pavia, Dana Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School, AdaptiveFlow allows prohibitively expensive ultra-large virtual drug screens to be conducted routinely. The open-source platform was published today in Nature Biotechnology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The fight to save Cavendish bananas as farms fall to Panama disease
item.description: Growers, researchers and plant breeders are looking for a genetically modified saviour for the world's most popular banana variety after the 11th detection of a soil-borne fungus in Queensland. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Sophie Johnson

item.title: Precision optics to make plant health visible from space
item.description: When the ESA Earth observation mission FLEX launches into space on September 15, 2026, as scheduled, it will carry high-precision optical components from Jena, Germany. Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Optics and Precision Engineering IOF have developed and manufactured a silicon-based double-slit assembly as well as two high-precision mirrors for the spectrometer on board the satellite. The spectrometer is designed to detect the fluorescence of plants excited by sunlight from Earth's orbit. The data is expected to provide new insights into the photosynthetic activity… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Larger catalyst batches could make carbon recycling cheaper and easier to scale
item.description: Turning carbon dioxide into industrial chemicals used in everything from synthetic fuels to plastics and pharmaceuticals is costly. But new research shows it does not have to be. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tests reveal how thermoplastic composites lose strength at elevated temperatures
item.description: Researchers from Skoltech together with colleagues from Xi'an Jiaotong University and the Blagonravov Institute of Mechanical Engineering of the Russian Academy of Sciences, have conducted a systematic study of the flexural properties of pultruded glass fiber composites based on three different thermoplastic matrices: polyphenylene sulfide (PPS), polyamide-6 (PA6) and polypropylene (PP). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers find dugong numbers halved in Gulf of Carpentaria
item.description: New research finds the number of dugongs in the Gulf of Carpentaria — one of the animal's most globally important populations — has halved in the past two decades, a decline scientists have called a "real shock". Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Warmer waters, pest species and habitat loss major threats to small, rare freshwater fish
item.description: One of Australia's most comprehensive assessments of endemic, rare or threatened freshwater fish has found numerous species are at severe risk of extinction because of multiple threats, including habitat loss, invasive species and warmer waters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Watching nanoparticles form in real time uncovers 'missing link' in microwave-assisted manufacturing
item.description: Advanced materials power everything from batteries and electronics to clean energy technologies. For years, engineers have known that microwave-assisted synthesis can dramatically accelerate the chemical reactions used to manufacture these materials. Now, researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have provided new evidence challenging a long-held assumption about why, suggesting that microwaves speed chemical reactions in a fundamentally different way than many scientists believed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Where people go shapes urban mixing more than where they live, research finds
item.description: For millennia, people have been drawn to cities for opportunities, jobs and the possibility of sharing a sidewalk with diverse and interesting groups of people. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cannabis ads may shape viewers' expectations about cannabis and sex
item.description: Alcohol advertisers have long faced industrywide guidelines discouraging them from linking drinking with sexual success. Cannabis marketers have no comparable industrywide guidelines and may promote cannabis in connection with sex and intimacy. A new Washington State University study suggests such messages may influence young adults' intentions to use cannabis before sex, with potential implications for sexual decision-making and consent. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What is public interest technology? An expert on data and policy explains how it helps people in need
item.description: Every year, millions of people who qualify for food assistance never get it. The money exists and they meet the eligibility rules, but they don't know that the program exists or whether they qualify. For others, the application is too long and complicated. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In tune with nature: Human speech follows a rhythm that is also found in the animal kingdom
item.description: The temporal structure of speech rhythms resembles that of the communication signals of numerous animal species. This is shown by a study conducted by a research team from the Leibniz Center for General Linguistics (ZAS) in Berlin, Humboldt Universität zu Berlin, the University of Regensburg and the Institute for Advanced Studies at Aix-Marseille University. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Martian astronomy: Percy sees a 'Phobos eclipse' from Mars
item.description: What's so special about spotting Phobos crossing in front of the sun? Sure. It's just another image of Phobos crossing the disk of the sun, as seen from the surface of Mars. Like so much of the modern space era, these images, once amazing, are now almost routine. But there's some real science behind tasking the Mars rovers to conduct a little "Martian astronomy." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hidden protein recycling hubs discovered inside human sperm cells
item.description: Researchers at VIB, VUB and the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology (UK) have discovered a hidden feature of human sperm cells. Using advanced imaging technologies, they discovered specialized compartments within the sperm nucleus packed with proteasomes, which are responsible for breaking down and recycling proteins. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What’s Up: September 2026 Skywatching Tips from NASA
item.description: Brilliant Venus and a Harvest Moon Use the Moon to find Antares and the Teapot, spot brilliant Venus, welcome the equinox, and see the Harvest Moon near Saturn and Neptune. Skywatching Highlights Transcript The Moon joins a tea party… Venus cranks up the brightness… the seasons officially change… and the Harvest Moon meets up with […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Switching gravity on and off leaves particles behind, mathematical model finds
item.description: Hawking radiation causes black holes to eventually evaporate. This is because particle pairs are spontaneously created near the event horizon (the position of the last ray of light that can escape the black hole's gravitational pull). A particle and its antiparticle are created for a brief moment and disappear immediately afterward. But sometimes a particle falls into the black hole, allowing the other particle to escape: This is Hawking radiation. According to Stephen Hawking, this would ultimately mean that no black holes would remain in the universe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Exposure to forever chemicals through sea spray may be overblown
item.description: Coastal residents may be worried about exposure to forever chemicals from sea spray during hot summer months, but York University researchers found little evidence of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) contamination from marine aerosols, a finding that surprised them. The study, published in Environmental Science: Processes & Impacts, looked specifically at areas affected by sea spray from the Atlantic Ocean generated by waves breaking along the coast of Newfoundland and Labrador. However, despite the region's windy, marine location, the researchers found it was not an issue as… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study: Reservoir management system could save California $150 million every year
item.description: A new study from the Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes (CW3E) at Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego finds that improved weather and water forecasts could help California gain more value from existing reservoirs and help meet a new water supply target. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First measurement of low-energy solar neutrinos scattering off electrons
item.description: Every second, tens of billions of neutrinos produced by nuclear fusion in the sun pass through every square centimeter of Earth—and through our bodies—almost without interacting. Although they are among the most abundant particles emitted by the sun, their extremely weak interactions make detecting these elusive particles one of the greatest experimental challenges in particle physics. A number of specialized neutrino detectors are in operation around the world, exploiting the unique properties of neutrinos to investigate astrophysical phenomena. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: MeerKAT directly detects faint hydrogen signal from the distant universe
item.description: Astronomers from the University of Manchester and the University of the Western Cape have directly detected an extremely faint radio signal from hydrogen gas billions of light-years away, opening a powerful new way to map the large-scale structure of the universe. Using South Africa's MeerKAT radio telescope, the international team measured radio emissions from neutral hydrogen dating back to a time when the universe was several billion years younger than it is today. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Remote work offers flexibility, but at the cost of learning opportunities for young workers
item.description: Six years after the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the shift to remote work, hybrid and remote arrangements have become an established part of the labor market. About one in five Canadians now works remotely some or all of the time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Diatom sequencing project finds striking genetic differences among microscopic algae
item.description: An international team of more than 100 scientists has taken a major step toward unlocking the secrets of some of Earth's tiniest but most important organisms. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New AI approaches to help understand complex biological data
item.description: Researchers at Cardiff University have presented two studies at the 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026) that address fundamental challenges in modern AI: understanding the complex geometry and relationships within data and recognizing patterns that occur across very different scales. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New AI model maps the ion binding sites that control how proteins work
item.description: Researchers at Constructor University and Constructor Labs have developed BiteNetI, a deep-learning model that locates the binding sites of 14 biologically important ion types directly in three-dimensional protein structures. The model needs only several seconds per structure and reaches two- to threefold higher accuracy than most existing predictors, including Google DeepMind's AlphaFold 3. The study, authored by Igor Kozlovskii and Petr Popov, has been published in the journal Communications Biology. The tool provides an open-access platform that could help accelerate drug discovery and the… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Historic Engines Take Their Place on Artemis III
item.description: On Aug. 24, technicians at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida began installing the four RS‑25 engines in the core stage of the agency’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket that will carry the Artemis III crew into low Earth orbit in 2027. Each RS‑25 engine has a unique serial number that records its detailed flight […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: AI tool detects unusual satellite behavior to improve space safety
item.description: A new AI model can monitor satellites and spot anomalies in their behavior, reducing the risk of in-orbit collisions, according to new research published in the journal Expert Systems. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ten-channel photonic interface links neutral-atom qubits in parallel
item.description: A research group in Japan has demonstrated a world-record 10-channel multiplexed quantum photonic interface based on an integrated waveguide array, a key technology for optically interconnecting multiple quantum computers. The study is published in the journal Optica. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Show HN: Newton's Orchard – Browser-based space/gravity playground
item.description: Hi HN! My son spent a lot of time in 5th grade playing with the 2-dimensional PhET gravity/space sims[1]. His STEM class uses it, and he was playing with it at home, and has been looking for more. I found several space sims/playgrounds online, including NASA's Eyes on the Solar System[2], but nothing that seemed to offer a real progression from what he was getting out of the PhET sims, so I built Newton's Orchard over the summer for him. https://newtonsorchard.app The source is also published at https://github.com/andrewchilds/newtons-orchard It features deterministic time scrubbing, all… Fuente: Hacker News - Portada.

item.title: 9/11 responders passed effects of trauma to their children, study finds
item.description: Although it's been 25 years since the World Trade Center collapsed after terrorists flew commercial airplanes into each of the center's two towers, the trauma experienced by many first responders and recovery workers is still being felt by their children. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Non-police safety practitioners reduce crime
item.description: Non-police community guardians can effectively reduce crime by building relationships in urban disorder hotspots, according to a study. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Geomagnetic superstorm shook GPS accuracy across the US—its timing may have averted agricultural losses
item.description: On Nov. 11, 2025, Earth experienced a severe geomagnetic storm triggered by solar flares and coronal mass ejections from an active sunspot region. While this kind of storm brings beautiful auroras admired in many areas around the world, it can also cause ionospheric disturbances that disrupt radio waves and affect crucial technologies. A new study, published in Geophysical Research Letters, found that disruptions caused by this storm scrambled GPS signals in areas where such disruptions have never been reported. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Largest review finds formal ethics education improves students' moral reasoning
item.description: How important is it that kids learn to tell right from wrong? Businessman and former university chancellor David Gonski recently called for ethics classes to be rolled out in all Australian schools to boost social cohesion. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Anti-influenza therapies that target the host
item.description: A drug that targets the host rather than the virus could get around the problem of antiviral resistance. Every year, hundreds of thousands of people die of seasonal influenza caused by infection with influenza A and B viruses. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Experiment sees surprising result in search for dark matter
item.description: For the better part of a century, people have been trying to understand dark matter. This invisible substance makes up roughly 85% of the mass in the universe but has never been directly detected. Determining exactly what it is remains one of the biggest questions about our world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: For a century, journalists have had a voluntary ethics code. Editors are giving it an AI-era reboot
item.description: Walk into a corner of a newsroom somewhere and you can often find it affixed to a bulletin board, perhaps peeking out from behind the coffee pot: the Society of Professional Journalists's Code of Ethics. It's less than a thousand words, fitting neatly on a poster. Publicado también por: The Independent - World. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ice island survives run-in with Joe Island
item.description: Summer is prime iceberg season in Greenland's glacier-fed fjords, and 2026 was no exception. Especially notable was the berg that broke from Petermann Glacier along Greenland's northwest coast in August. Roughly the size of St. Thomas in the U.S. Virgin Islands, it was the largest calving event by any Arctic glacier since 2020. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Warming winters weaken New Hampshire forest's carbon sink over 20 years
item.description: Can we count on forests to continue absorbing the carbon dioxide that's warming our world? A new study from researchers at NAU and the University of New Hampshire says ... maybe not. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Peacemaker program linked to 61% decline in gun violence deaths and injuries
item.description: A new study by researchers at UC Berkeley's Center for Global Healthy Cities, published in JAMA Network Open, found that the California city of Richmond's Office of Neighborhood Safety (ONS) was responsible for a 61% reduction in the city's firearm homicides and injury shootings over the past 14 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Marmite lures discovery from lake depths
item.description: Dr. Roe Stuart didn't find a taniwha in the unexplored depths of New Zealand's lakes—but they may have found a new species of fish. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ultrafast snapshots reveal the first moments on the way from light to electricity
item.description: Physicists at the University of Graz (Austria), in collaboration with colleagues from Marburg University and Forschungszentrum Jülich (Germany), have achieved a scientific breakthrough. For the first time, the generation of electrical energy from light has been filmed and described theoretically. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Screening tool amplifies tiny changes in protein levels within cells
item.description: Imagine a brain teaser where the challenge is to spot the difference between two nearly identical sandcastles. The only difference? The removal of three grains of sand. Scientists face a similarly exasperating challenge when looking at changes in protein levels within our cells, where small fluctuations can mean the difference between health and disease or a drug working and not working. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: The first thing that struck us wasn't the missing trees, but the missing water. In May 2026, we visited the Sundarbans, a mangrove forest in the delta where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers meet in the Bay of Bengal. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Q&A: Can you trust online ratings in the age of 'review bombing'?
item.description: Before buying a product, booking a hotel or streaming a movie, many people check online reviews. But not every glowing recommendation or one-star takedown reflects a genuine customer experience. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Resin-mounted wallaby teeth reveal rare 1,200-year-old ornaments in Queensland
item.description: While sorting through animal bones in a rock shelter in Queensland, Australia, archaeologists came across a tooth where something was "not quite right." Stuck to the tip of its root was a blackish-brown ball of glue-like resin. Eleven more teeth with the same sticky substance were found, making them the only known instance of this type of tooth ornament found outside burials in northeastern Australia and the first in the Cape York Peninsula (CYP), the new study published in Australian Archaeology reports. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Three common study myths busted by a learning expert—and better strategies to use instead
item.description: As high school and university students approach exam periods, study sessions often increase in frequency and intensity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Old-growth tropical forests bear lasting legacy of ancient Maya civilization
item.description: Rainforests in Central America that have remained largely untouched by modern human activities could bear the invisible imprint of ancient Maya civilizations. New research has found that forest structure in Belize, such as canopy height and leaf density, may be influenced by how the Maya transformed and used the land thousands of years ago. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fieldwork safety emerges as a structural challenge for ecological research
item.description: A new Viewpoint in the journal BioScience argues that gender-based and sexual violence (GBSV) in ecological fieldwork should be understood not as a series of isolated incidents but as a structural problem rooted in how field research is organized, with broad consequences for the knowledge such research produces. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: A lack of central oversight and shifting catering models in primary schools could be putting children's dietary health at risk, according to new research led by the University of York. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Some of Australia's biggest companies are planning for an unbearable climate future
item.description: Even as unprecedented fires and heat waves rage across Europe, scientists track the retreat of Antarctic sea ice and a supercharged El Niño system heads our way, Australia's largest companies are forecasting business as usual in a much hotter world. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Growing bacteria line up single-file, then buckle in liquid crystals
item.description: When scientists study bacteria that are not in a Petri dish or a test tube but in environments that more closely mimic their actual microbial habitats, they often find delightfully unexpected behaviors. For Sujit Datta, a professor of chemical engineering, bioengineering and biophysics at Caltech, those oddities are an invitation to apply physics to exciting new puzzles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drone laser scans map more than 1,000 trees across 90-acre campus
item.description: It took one drone, 300 million laser data points and seven teams of students on foot to map Wake Forest University's trees. Led by Ovidiu Csillik, an assistant professor of remote sensing in the environment and sustainability studies program, the project produced a publicly accessible, interactive 3D digital map of more than 1,000 trees and helped the university earn international accreditation as a Level II arboretum. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Starship could create more debris than an anti-satellite test if it explodes in orbit
item.description: As Starship, the world’s largest and most powerful rocket, gears up for an attempt to finally reach Earth’s orbit, experts say the risk of an in-flight catastrophe – and a cloud of debris – “needs to be of concern”. Elon Musk’s SpaceX is expected to launch the Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy booster for the launch system’s 14th test flight and first orbital test flight later this month. According to one aerospace expert, if the Starship’s upper stage explodes in orbit it could produce debris... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Bees see the world in more ways than previously thought
item.description: The honey bee has held a special place in vision research. It is one of the best-studied insects, and much of what scientists know about how bees perceive the world is based on studies of honey bees. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mindfulness may lower blood pressure in just 8 weeks
item.description: Mindfulness, gratitude, and optimism training may improve blood pressure, inflammation, and other heart-health measures within just eight to 12 weeks. The strongest programs paired daily practice with regular reinforcement, suggesting that improving psychological well-being could become another tool for protecting cardiovascular health. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A supermassive black hole erupted in X-rays, and its radio jets followed 300 days later
item.description: By combining roughly two decades of observations from NASA's Swift X-ray Telescope with radio monitoring, astronomers have caught a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Perseus Cluster suddenly flaring in X-rays, and about 300 days later, its powerful radio emission flared too. Their paper describing the connection between this black hole's accretion disk and the jets it launches was submitted to the arXiv preprint server on Aug. 13 and accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover why snake embryos twist into spirals
item.description: Snake embryos begin life curled into a distinctive right-handed spiral, and scientists may finally know why. Their bodies grow faster than their guts, creating a tether that forces the lengthening embryo to buckle and twist inside the egg. Researchers reached the conclusion after studying more than 900 embryos and using CT scans to reveal the hidden anatomy behind the coils. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Research highlights hidden impact of domestic violence on women and their pets
item.description: New research from James Cook University has found that women experiencing domestic violence are often forced to choose between their own safety and the safety of their pets, with limited pet-inclusive crisis support contributing to additional trauma and distress. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reaching 90 without dementia doesn’t mean you’re in the clear
item.description: A study of people over 90 found that dementia risk remains strongly shaped by sex, race and genetics, with women and black participants facing notably higher risks. Intriguingly, some people stayed cognitively healthy despite carrying major risk factors, potentially offering clues to how the brain can resist dementia deep into old age. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: When exposed to air, new nanomaterial becomes magnetic at high temperatures
item.description: While fridge magnets are great for saving favorite recipes, modern magnetic materials are useful for improving fiber optics or quantum information science technology. On most fridge magnets the atoms are arranged in a repeated lattice structure called a "spinel." These structures are made up of three types of atoms, generically referred to as atoms "A," "B" and "X." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: UK researchers made a reef from 50 tonnes of coal waste; marine life arrived within 3 weeks
item.description: Researchers created an artificial reef from coal-fired power station waste in Poole Bay. Marine life began colonizing the structure almost immediately after its deployment. Adult lobsters and edible crabs reached the reef within three weeks of its placement. The structure attracted schools of pouting and supported reproduction for several species. This experiment showed industrial waste could become a productive marine habitat. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How do you get middle schoolers to eat more fruit? Give them smoothies
item.description: At lunchtime in rural Maine middle schools, University of Maine researchers stood at two points in the cafeteria. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 12,000-year-old skeletons in Italy reveal a mother-daughter relationship
item.description: Archaeologists discovered two skeletons in an embrace within Romito Cave over twelve thousand years ago. Genetic analysis revealed these individuals were both female and closely related, likely mother and daughter. The younger skeleton showed a rare inherited disorder affecting growth and limb development. This finding confirms the existence of genetic diseases in ancient human populations. The discovery also suggests prehistoric communities provided care for individuals with physical limitations. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Engagement-driven curation can trap culture consumers in 'overfamiliarity,' leading to less long-term satisfaction
item.description: Sometimes you can be too good at your job. Take streaming services, like Spotify or Netflix. With engagement as their main goal, their recommendation algorithms typically identify the content a user engaged with most in the recent past and efficiently suggest more of the same. Content and genres that received limited engagement over a few weeks or months typically get dropped. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A massive plume deep beneath Africa is pulling the continent apart
item.description: A vast plume rising from deep inside Earth may be responsible for mysterious movements along the East African Rift. The discovery reveals how forces deep in the mantle are working alongside shallower geological forces as the continent slowly pulls apart. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: In Japan's mountains, a different way to manage bears
item.description: As a sensor sounded, scientist Akiko Takii hurried to a bear trap deep in the forests of Nagano, Japan, where rising nationwide attacks have sparked fear and the culling of thousands of the animals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Samba’s fiery farewell recorded
item.description: Yesterday, on 31 August 2026, Samba reentered Earth’s atmosphere at 21:39:38 UTC / 23:39:38 CEST as the third of the four Cluster satellites. Samba had been lined up for a special 'targeted reentry' safely over the South Pacific Ocean, the precision so high that a plane could fly out from Tonga and successfully record its demise for reentry science. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Food innovation in your kitchen: Giving peas, beans and lentils a surprisingly meat-like bite
item.description: Separating things and then putting them back together is a common principle in industrial food production. Agricultural raw materials are broken down into their individual constituents, such as proteins, starches and fats, and the food industry then reassembles these building blocks into specific products. In many cases, not all of the harvested crop ends up in the food we eat. In some instances, byproducts are formed that must be reused outside the food industry. These processing steps can also lead to the loss of dietary fibers, vitamins and minerals in the finished product. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Declining star formation not caused by simple 'fuel crisis,' new measurements suggest
item.description: The universe has been having fewer and fewer stellar "babies." Over the past 4.5 billion years, the rate of star birth has crashed to less than half of what it once was. But here's the twist: the most essential "fuel" for making stars has barely decreased. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Researchers catch sharks off NY's Hamptons, attach trackers to toothy predators
